_comment: The single source of truth for which sky cultures are kept OUT of every
public deployment of this project. Read by deploy/exclusions.sh (the two
shell deploy paths) and deploy/filter_taxonomy.py (the culture tree), so
no deploy path can drift from another on a licence question.
Reusing an excluded culture's data SHAPE is fine; copying its CONTENT is
not. Both licence exclusions are reversible by asking the authors, and
that ask is worth making — see docs/GOVERNANCE.md.
'reason' is rendered in the deployed UI, so it must be accurate and
must not imply the community has no sky knowledge recorded. It has;
we are the ones without permission to redistribute it.
'bundled_skycultures_allowed' covers a SECOND, easily-missed source of
cultural content: the engine's own demo data (web/public/skydata/) ships
sky cultures of its own, and both deploy paths copy that directory
wholesale. The 'cultures' list above only ever guarded the FETCHED set in
web/public/skycultures/, so anything riding along inside skydata was
published unexamined and unattributed.
This is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist, on purpose: it names what the app
actually loads, so a future skydata refresh that adds a culture fails the
build instead of silently publishing it.
'unattributed_surveys' is a THIRD source of content, found the same way
the belarusian sky culture was: web/public/skydata is copied wholesale by
both deploy paths, so anything dropped in there ships. Mirrored HiPS
surveys land in skydata/surveys/ and would go out unexamined.

cultures.reason: Not shown in this deployment. Its licence (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) grants redistribution permission to the Stellarium developers specifically, and this project is not that party. The data exists and is published upstream — we lack permission to republish it here.

This project's own throwaway demo export from testing the authoring round-trip. Not real cultural content, and must never be published as though it were.

_bundled_note: Only 'western' is allowed because engine.js boots exactly one bundled culture (core.skycultures.addDataSource with key 'western'). Anything else in skydata/skycultures/ is unreachable in the UI, absent from the attribution panel, and therefore published with no credit shown. The 'belarusian' culture was in exactly that state and its own description.md states 'Text and data: TODO' -- upstream has not determined a licence for it, so we certainly cannot assert one by republishing it.
_surveys_note: Mirrored from data.stellarium.org for local development. NOT shipped: their properties files carry no obs_copyright, no obs_ack and no hips_creator, there is no README or LICENSE alongside them on the server, and nothing in the engine repository records what they were built from. The designations they carry (Messier, NGC, IC) are historical catalogues, but the compiled positions, magnitudes and morphologies are somebody's work and we cannot say whose. Publishing 34.7 MB of it with no credit is the belarusian mistake again. Resolve with upstream before shipping; until then the app falls back to the engine's own bundled dso survey, which ships with it.
